explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The LORD says, "The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time." (Numbers 9:2) Notice the words "appointed time." This feast has a date on the calendar, and it's not a suggestion. Moses, Israel's leader, gets the word straight from the LORD.

Jubilee is a different thing, friend. Here the LORD says, "The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time." (Numbers 9:2) The Jubilee never comes up in these verses. This whole passage is about one feast and its date on the calendar.

I see why you'd go there, because the Sabbath is a big deal too. But the LORD tells Moses, "The Israelites are to observe the Passover at its appointed time." (Numbers 9:2) The Sabbath isn't mentioned in this passage. Everything here points to Passover and when it happens.

True! The text says, "The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 9:5) It happened in the Wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. Everything, friend. I can't even get my dough chilled on time, and they did EVERYTHING.

Look at the verse again, friend. It says, "The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 9:5) That's the Wilderness of Sinai, twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. They did it, start to finish. Me? I once stamped a whole batch upside down and called it a design choice.

explanations.answer: They are unclean due to a dead body
explanations.explanation: Right on the money. The text says these men "…were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day." (Numbers 9:6) Nothing in the text says they did anything wrong, and I'm not going to add anything to it. They were stuck, plain and simple.

explanations.answer: They are serving at the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but that's not in the text. Numbers 9:6 says these men "…were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day." Serving at the Tent isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses. The reason is the dead body, and that's all the text gives.

explanations.answer: They have no lamb for the meal
explanations.explanation: The lamb isn't the problem here, friend. The text says these men "…were unclean due to a dead body, so they could not observe the Passover on that day." (Numbers 9:6) Nobody mentions a missing lamb. If I tried to blame the lamb, I'd be making things up, and I only bake with what's written.

explanations.answer: Why they should be left out of presenting the LORD's offering
explanations.explanation: That's it. They say, "We are unclean because of a dead body, but why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" (Numbers 9:7) They name the problem up front and then ask the question anyway. I think that took some nerve, and I admire it. They wanted in, friend.

explanations.answer: Whether someone else could eat their share of the meal
explanations.explanation: The men ask something different. They say, "…why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" (Numbers 9:7) Their question is about being left out of the offering. Nothing in the verse mentions someone else eating their share.

explanations.answer: Whether they could leave the camp until the feast was over
explanations.explanation: Close, friend, but that's not their question. They say, "…why should we be excluded from presenting the LORD’s offering with the other Israelites at the appointed time?" (Numbers 9:7) Their words are about the offering and being excluded from it. Leaving the camp isn't in what they ask.

explanations.answer: He tells them to wait while he finds out what the LORD commands
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Moses says, "Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you…" (Numbers 9:8) He doesn't make up an answer on the spot. I'd have panicked and handed them a cookie. Moses waits for the LORD's word.

explanations.answer: He tells them to sit this year out and try again next year
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't say that, friend. He says, "Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you…" (Numbers 9:8) He has no answer yet, so he goes to find out. The LORD speaks next in verse 9.

explanations.answer: He tells them to go wash their clothes and join in tonight
explanations.explanation: That would be a quick fix, but it's not what Moses says. He tells them, "Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands concerning you…" (Numbers 9:8) Moses doesn't hand out a ruling of his own. He waits for the LORD to answer.

That's the one. The LORD says that anyone "…unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD." (Numbers 9:10) So the men asked about one situation, and the answer covers a second one too. The LORD gave more than they asked for.

Sickness isn't on the list, friend. The LORD says, "…is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD." (Numbers 9:10) The second situation is the journey. I'm not going to add one the text doesn't have.

Close to the idea of being away, but the text doesn't say that. The LORD says, "…or is away on a journey, he may still observe the Passover to the LORD." (Numbers 9:10) The word is journey. Fieldwork never shows up in these verses.

Yes, the second month. The LORD says, "Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month." (Numbers 9:11) Same day number, one month later. The men got a real way back in.

Not the third, friend. The text says, "Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month." (Numbers 9:11) It's the same fourteenth day, just one month later than the first. Only one extra month, no more.

That's a long wait, and the text doesn't give it. It says, "Such people are to observe it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month." (Numbers 9:11) The second month, friend. Six months of waiting would be rough on anybody.

Careful with this one, friend. The LORD says that those who keep the later Passover "…must observe the Passover according to all its statutes." (Numbers 9:12) All of them. They also eat the lamb with unleavened bread and bitter herbs (Numbers 9:11), and they may not leave any of it until morning or break any of its bones. So it's the same rules, not a lighter set.

Right, it's false. The LORD says, "They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes." (Numbers 9:12) They eat the lamb with unleavened bread and bitter herbs (Numbers 9:11), leave none of it until morning and break none of its bones. A later date, but the same rules.

explanations.answer: He must be cut off from his people
explanations.explanation: That's what the text says. "…if a man who is ceremonially clean and is not on a journey still fails to observe the Passover, he must be cut off from his people…" (Numbers 9:13) Notice the two conditions: ceremonially clean and not on a journey. It's a serious line, so I'll just say it plainly. The text says he must be cut off.

explanations.answer: He keeps it in the next month instead
explanations.explanation: The second month is for a different kind of person, friend. Verses 10 and 11 give it to someone unclean because of a dead body or away on a journey. For a man who is ceremonially clean and not on a journey, the text says, "…he must be cut off from his people…" (Numbers 9:13) This one is heavy, so let's take it seriously.

explanations.answer: He brings a double offering next year
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention a double offering. It says, "…he must be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD’s offering at its appointed time." (Numbers 9:13) That's a serious word, so I'll stick to just what the verse says.

True, friend. The LORD says, "You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land." (Numbers 9:14) A foreigner dwelling among them who wants to observe the Passover to the LORD does it by the Passover statute and its ordinances. One statute for both.

Not false, friend. The LORD says the foreigner "…is to do so according to the Passover statute and its ordinances." (Numbers 9:14) He adds, "You are to apply the same statute to both the foreigner and the native of the land." One statute covers both.
